reading.body:
itQ Data Center is a plausible but unconfirmed small facility in Wrocław, Poland, with no capacity figure attached to it.

The record is an OpenStreetMap entry tagged as a data center, named itQ Data Center, with a website on the .pl domain and a location in Wrocław. The name itself is the strongest signal here: it states IT and data-center services directly rather than hinting at them. Wrocław is a real technology and outsourcing hub, so a small operator there is not implausible on its face.

What the data does not contain is anything that would let a reader size the facility. There is no megawatt figure, no operator name, no confirmed business registration, and no press coverage. The research status is exhausted, meaning the entry was filed without verification rather than cleared. For AI infrastructure questions, that absence matters more than the name: a data center with no published power draw cannot be placed on any compute curve, and a single unverified building tells you nothing about regional capacity.

The honest reading is that this is a lead, not a data point. It confirms only that a facility calling itself a data center exists at a mapped location near Copernicus Wrocław Airport, roughly 6.8 miles away. Whether it holds racks, how much power it draws, and who runs it remain open.
